note: Each case: a temp source project (the committed v3 fixture bytes) + a temp backup/destination state, the procedure invoked, the expected code, and the original-preservation assertion (the source tree is byte-identical after the refusal — the acceptance obligation: "fixtures prove refusals retain originals"). The checker runs every case through its reference implementation of the §1–§2 procedures.

cases.setup: a backup dir whose scenes/main.json is truncated (last 100 bytes removed)
cases.originals: the source project untouched (verify is read-only on the backup; the source is never read by verify)

cases.setup: a backup dir whose project.json has one flipped byte (the manifest byteLength unchanged)

a backup dir whose inventory names a sources/sha256/<d> file that is absent, AND the envelope catalog names that digest (a temp catalog extension — the generator materializes a temp project with one published blob and the backup omits it)
cases.originals: the source project (with its blob) untouched

cases.setup: a temp project whose catalog carries versions 1 AND 2 of one asset (two digests); the backup omits the v1 file
cases.expected: backup_blob_missing (superseded: true — the §15 "every file, including superseded versions" rule)
cases.originals: the source project (both blob files) untouched

cases.setup: a backup dir whose inventory includes a .thirdlight/ownership.json path
a backup (verified) + a destination project dir that already exists with a byte in it
cases.originals: the existing destination byte-identical + the source backup untouched

cases.setup: a backup dir whose inventory path is ../../etc/passwd (an escape)
the source project with a LIVE ownership record (owned, holder pid = a real live process — the checker records its own pid)
cases.originals: the source project byte-identical (the refusal is before any read-copy); a second run with the record marked stale proceeds (the accepted §6.2 rule)
